learnings.question: In the 1880s, a psychologist demonstrated that people forget roughly what percentage of newly learned information within just 24 hours, unless they actively recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus showed in the 1880s that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it — the basis for spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term, coined by researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper, describes the tendency to forget information as soon as it's saved digitally or looked up online?
learnings.learning: The 'Google Effect' research calls it Digital Amnesia: the moment we write something down or save it digitally, our brains treat that as permission to forget it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, what is the name of the artifact that visualizes a Sprint's progress and shows how much work remains?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is the Scrum artifact that visualizes Sprint progress, showing remaining work and whether the team is on schedule.

learnings.question: Which job title is commonly mistaken for an official Scrum role, despite not actually being one of Scrum's three defined roles?
learnings.learning: Scrum defines only three roles — Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers. 'Project Manager' is not one of them, a common point of confusion for people new to the framework.

learnings.question: What Arabic term, drawn from Quran 2:30, refers to humanity's role as steward or caretaker of the Earth?
learnings.learning: Khalifah is the Quranic term (2:30) for humanity's role as steward or caretaker of the Earth, carrying responsibility for preserving faith and unity.

learnings.question: According to Surah Adh-Dhariyat (51:56), what is given as the core reason jinn and mankind were created?
options: To multiply and populate the earth
To seek knowledge above all else
learnings.learning: Quran 51:56 states: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me' — framed as the foundational purpose of human existence.

learnings.question: Which Hadith collection records the Prophet Muhammad's (ﷺ) statement, 'There will be no prophet after me; instead, there will be caliphs'?
learnings.learning: The statement 'There will be no prophet after me; instead, there will be caliphs' is recorded in Sahih Bukhari 3455, underscoring the responsibility of continued leadership after the Prophet.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state represents a device fully powered on and actively transmitting data, with no power-saving measures applied?
learnings.learning: L0 is the PCIe active state: the device is fully operational and transmitting data, with no power-saving measures in effect.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: What is given as the primary purpose of implementing power management states in PCIe devices?
options: Increasing the raw physical data-transfer speed between devices
Efficient energy use, extending device longevity, and enhancing system performance
Enabling backward compatibility with USB devices
Reducing the manufacturing cost of PCIe hardware
learnings.learning: PCIe power management states exist to efficiently manage energy use, extend device longevity, and enhance system performance, especially where power consumption is a major concern.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to the actual unfolding of events in a person's life, as opposed to Allah's complete eternal foreknowledge of them?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in our lives as they unfold, shaped by our actions — distinct from Qadr, which is Allah's complete, eternal plan.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Which Quranic verse teaches that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves?
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11 teaches that Allah does not change a people's condition until they change what is within themselves — framed as the basis for taking responsibility for one's own Qada'.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: What resolves the apparent tension between making Dua to change one's circumstances and Allah's complete, eternal foreknowledge of all events?
options: Any change brought about through Dua was already known by Allah and is itself part of His Qadr
Qada' and Qadr are simply two names for the same fixed, unchangeable outcome
Dua only brings spiritual reward and has no effect on worldly outcomes
Free will is an illusion, so no action, including Dua, changes anything
learnings.learning: Dua and action can alter one's Qada', but that very change was always encompassed within Allah's Qadr — His perfect, prior knowledge — resolving the tension between free will and predestination.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In a word-frequency analysis of the Quran testing the 80/20 Pareto Principle, what percentage of the Quran's total text did the top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: Contrary to the 80/20 Pareto Principle hypothesis, the top 20 most frequent words in the Quran accounted for only about 20.83% of its total text, not 80%.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: In Arabic script, what term refers to the small diacritical marks placed above or below letters to indicate vowel sounds?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the small diacritical marks added above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds, similar to how vowels work in English.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: When analyzing word frequency across the Quran, why was the original Arabic text used instead of an English translation?
options: Because Arabic text requires less computational processing power to analyze
Because English translations aren't a direct equivalent, and Arabic has a far larger vocabulary (around 12 million words) than English (around 170,000)
Because the Quran.com API only accepts Arabic-language queries
Because no English translation of the Quran has ever been published
learnings.learning: Arabic was chosen over English translation because translations aren't a direct equivalent, and Arabic's vocabulary (roughly 12 million words) vastly outnumbers English's (roughly 170,000 words in the Oxford English Dictionary) — about a 71:1 ratio.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
